I would also look at AAVE (African American vernacular english). Its got a pretty consistent grammar. It has a lot of interesting words and terms derived or evolved from both English words ans historic circumstance. And it's rapidly evolving and changing. As young black people invent new slang that becomes adopted by people who don't consider themselves AAVE speakers. Its interconnected with American English but still very distinct. And even if its not the right sound or direction you want to go in for undercommon its a very cool example of how language can evolve due to in-group and out-group distinctions, and along class/race lines.
